Mr. Shamsul Alam, D.A.G ------ For the Appellant. 
Mr. S.R. Pal with Mr. Abdul Quium and Mr. M.A. Noor ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Chief Engineer, Roads & Highways Departments
Vs.
M/s. Concord Engineer Limited Construction
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This First Miscellaneous Appeal at the instance of the second party appellant is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.11.1992 passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous case No. 71 of 1991 making the award dated 21.2.1991 given by the sole arbitrator Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan, rule of the Court. 

 3. The concerned Executive Engineer by his Memo dated 20.4.1991 also requested the respondent Concord Engineers to furnish all related documents and explanations in support of their claim to facilitate/ determination of the same by the Additional Chief Engineer. The respondent without complying with the said request of the Additional Chief Engineer wrote to the Chief Engineer invoking clause B.6. 31 of the agreement and requested him to appoint arbitrator on his behalf in the matter informing him that they had already appointed Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as their arbitrator in the matter to settle the dispute between the parties as the Additional Chief Engineer did not settle the dispute. The Chief Engineer on receipt of the letter dated 29.4.1991 did not appoint any arbitrator on his behalf and after waiting for six weeks the respondent requested their appointed arbitrator to start arbitration proceeding as sole arbitrator. In that view of the matter the arbitrator appointed by the respondent as per provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1940, assumed jurisdiction in the instant case as sole arbitrator and notified both the parties to appear before him and submit their case in writing. It appears that the respondent in pursuance of that notice appeared before the arbitrator and submitted their statement of claim. On the other hand, the appellant prayed for time but subsequently they did neither file any written objection nor participated in the proceedings and in that view of the matter the arbitrator concluded the proceeding ex-parte against the appellant and gave an award amounting to Tk. 15 crore and odd as compensation to respondent. The learned arbitrator signed and delivered the award on 21.9.91 with notice to both the parties but the appellant did not appear before the arbitrator nor signed the award. After the pronouncement of the said award, the arbitrator sent the same to the Court of the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka on 6.10.91 for making the said award a rule of the Court. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing both the parties and perusing the relevant documents and the award made the award rule of the court vide his judgment dated 30.11.92 on the ground that the objection filed by the appellant under section 16 and 31 of the said Act were absolutely misconceived. The learned Subordinate Judge further found that the objection, if any, in the instant case could have been filed under section 33 read with section 30 of the Act but instead of that they have filed an objection under section 16 read with section 31 of the said Act which is not tenable in law in the facts and circumstances of the case. The learned Subordinate Judge further travelled to observe that even if for argument's sake it is assumed that the said objection was in fact filed under section 33 read with section 30 of the Act then also the same is not acceptable on two counts; firstly it is barred by limitation as provided by article 158 of the Limitation Act and secondly for non compliance of the proviso to section 33 the Act which has been added to it after the amendment of the aforesaid section by virtue of provision of law Reforms Ordinance, 1978. The learned Subordinate Judge also perused the records of the arbitration case and the award itself and did not find anything on record to interfere with the award declared by the learned arbitrator and in that view of the matter made the award rule of the court by the impugned judgment and order dated 30.11.92. Being aggrieved by the said judgment the second party appellant preferred this appeal. 

 6. Mr. Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the appellant, submits that the award in question is a nullity in the eye of law inasmuch as the arbitrator was not appointed as per terms of the arbitration clause embodied in the instant contract dated 3.9.90 and as such it is void abinitio and has got no existence of its own in the eye of law. The learned D.A.G. further submits that in making the award rule of the court the learned Subordinate Judge lost sight of the fact that the learned arbitrator Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan does not answer description of the arbitrator as contemplated in the arbitration clause of the agreement and in that view of the matter also the arbitrator had no authority to arbitrate upon in the instant case. The learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that it is true that in the written objection filed by the appellant before the subordinate Judge they misquoted section 16 and 31 of the Arbitration Act but this alone cannot be a ground for throwing away the objection on this technical ground without entering into merits of the case and on that count also the impugned order is not sustainable in law. Mr. Shamsul Alam further submits that since the appointment of Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as an arbitrator/ sole arbitrator in the matter was made by the respondent unilaterally and in contravention of the terms of the contract dated 3.9.1990 particularly clause B.6.31 of the Tender Document and clause 25 of Bangladesh Tender Form No. 2911 as amended on 23.9.1987 the proceedings conducted by Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan is without jurisdiction and a nullity in the eye of law. Mr. Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney General further submits that in view of the admitted fact that Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan was not appointed as an arbitrator under clause B.6.31 of the contract as well as Bangladesh Form No. 2211 as amended upto date nor does he fit in the description of person/ persons to be appointed as an Arbitrator, the award made by Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan is illegal and without jurisdiction and the learned Subordinate Judge ought to have, under section 17 of the Arbitration Act, set aside the award suo motu without waiting for any objection to the award being filed or without considering any application for setting it aside. The learned Deputy Attorney General also submits that the award in question is illegal and void for want of jurisdiction apparent on the fact of it, it is not necessary that parties should file objection to the alleged award, within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the limitation Act and the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in holding that the objection filed by the opposite party appellant long after 20 days is hopelessly barred by limitation. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge erred in law in not considering the arbitration agreement in order to determine as to whether the parties agreed to refer their dispute to Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan for arbitration. The learned Deputy Attorney General finally submits that the learned Subordinate Judge failed to appreciate the point in issue or in other words he failed to perceive whether the alleged award is an "award" as defined in section 2(b) of the Arbitration Act and also whether the same could he filed .under section 14 of the Arbitration Act. 

 7. Mr. S.R. Pal, the learned Advocate appearing for the first party respondent, submits that the appellant at this belated stage cannot call in question the legality or validity of the award given by the sole arbitrator in the instant case inasmuch as they submitted written objection against the aforesaid award before the learned Subordinate Judge not under section 33 read with section 30 of the Act rather they filed it under section 16 read with section 31 of the Arbitration Act and the learned Sub-ordinate Judge taking a correct view of law has rightly rejected the written objection on cogent and valid ground which cannot be assailed on any ground whatsoever. Mr. Pal further submits with much emphasis that the question of jurisdiction or authority of the arbitrator to arbitrate the instant dispute cannot be raised by the appellant before this court for the first time as they did not raise any such objection either before the learned Arbitrator or before the learned Subordinate Judge in their written objection and they had in fact submitted to the jurisdiction of the arbitrator by once applying for time to file written objection and, thus, it must be presumed in the facts and circumstances of the instant case that the right to challenge the authority of the arbitrator, if any, had been waived and acquiescenced by the appellant in the instant case. Mr. Pal further submits that the appellant now also cannot argue on the validity or legality of the award inasmuch as in their alleged written objection they had in fact only called in question the quantum of Taka 16 crore and odd as awarded by the Arbitrator and prayed to the court to remit the award to the Arbitrator to substract certain amount from the amount given in the award but they did not attack the award on the ground of misconduct. Mr. Pal further submits that it is apparent from the prayer made by the appellant in their written objection that they had submitted to the jurisdiction of the arbitrator because their sole objection was to the effect that the arbitrator has given an amount to the tune of Taka 15 crore and odd which amount is unreasonable. Mr. Pal further submitted that the alleged objection be it under section 16 read with section 31 or section 33 read with section 30 is barred by limitation inasmuch as in both the cases it is governed by article 158 of the Limitation Act which provides a limitation of 30 days from the date of submission of the award to the court. Mr. S.R. Pal further submits that this written objection is not sustainable in law inasmuch as in filing this written objection the appellant has filed to comply with the proviso to section 33 of the amended Act which provides that at the time of filing of the written objection the aggrieved party must furnish either in cash the amount awarded by the arbitrator to the court or security to the satisfaction of the court for awarded amount but in the instant case they have neither deposited money nor security to the satisfaction of the Court and in that view of the matter the written objection has no existence in the eye of law and that is not an objection in the eye of law and for this purpose Mr. Pal relied on the case of Director General / Chairman Bangladesh Television Versus Bengal Techno Consult Limited an unreported decision of this Court wherein it has been held that non-compliance of the proviso of section 33 of the Act rendered the objection a nullity in the eye of law. 

 8. There is no dispute that there is an arbitration clause in the instant contract. In this case it is also admitted that the award was sent in the court on 6.10.1991 and the appellant appeared before the Court on 3.11.91 and filed the written objection on 21.3.1992 and it is thus apparent that the written objection filed by the appellant against the award is barred by limitation as they have failed to file the same within 30 days from the date of submission of the award to the court. Article 158 of the Limitation Act is very clear on this point. It is also admitted by both the sides that at the time of submitting the written objection before the Subordinate Judge the appellant did not file the amount of the award in cash to the court nor they furnished any security to the satisfaction of the Court. Proviso to section 33 that is the amended section 33 has been interpreted by another Division Bench of this Court wherein their Lordships have held that non-compliance of the proviso of section 33 would render the objection a nullity in the eye of law and that objection must be treated as no objection at all. Similar view is taken by another Division Bench in the case reported in 1988 BLD. 364. 

 "Settlement of disputes: All disputes of any kind whatsoever arising out of connected with the contract shall be referred to the Additional Chief Engineer for settlement. If either the Engineer or Engineer-in-Charge or the contractor be dissatisfied with the decision of the Additional Chief Engineer on any matter of dispute the employer or the Contractor may within 20 days after receiving notice of such decision give a written notice to the other part requiring that the matter in dispute be arbitrated upon. In such case the present rules of the RHD for arbitration will be followed i.e. as per clause 25 of the Bangladesh form No. 2911 with amendment dated 23.9.87." 

 10. On perusal of the arbitration clause it appears that if any dispute or difference arise between the parties toughing any matter of the agreement the aggrieved party will refer it to the Additional Chief Engineer and if any party is aggrieved by the decision of the Additional Chief Engineer he may refer the matter to the Chief Engineer within 20 days from the date of decision requesting the Chief Engineer to appoint arbitrator/ arbitrators as designated in clause B.6.31 of the Contract. It appears from the record that in the instant case after cancellation of the agreement by the appellant, respondent wrote a letter to the Additional Chief Engineer claiming compensation to the tune of Taka 30 crore and odd and on receipt of the said letter the Additional Chief Engineer requested the respondent to file supporting documents but the respondent without complying with that request wrote a letter to the Chief Engineer intimating him that they have appointed Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as their arbitrator and requested the Chief Engineer to appoint an arbitrator on his behalf to settle the dispute that arose between the parties due to the unilateral cancellation of the contract by the appellant at the directive of the Government. It, however, appears that the Chief Engineer after receipt of the said letter for reason best known to him did not appoint any arbitrator or arbitrators as contemplated in the arbitration clause of the agreement. In the event of failure of the Chief Engineer to appoint an arbitrator or arbitrators in the instant case the respondent had no other alternative but to appoint Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as their arbitrator and notified the appellant to appoint their arbitrator to resolve the dispute between the parties but in-spite of this notice they have failed to appoint any arbitrator on their behalf. Thereafter the arbitrator appointed by the respondent after the lapse of about six weeks assumed jurisdiction in the matter as sole arbitrator and notified the parties to submit their case before him in writing. In response to the notice of the arbitrator, the respondent appeared before the arbitrator and submitted their statement of claims. On the other hand, the appellant had sent a letter stating that 25.6.1991 being a holiday no action could be taken on that day and they required instruction from the authorities but subsequently they did neither file any written objection nor participated in the proceeding and as such the sole arbitrator had no other alternative but to proceed ex-parte in the matter and ultimately after hearing the respondent and perusing their papers delivered and signed the relevant award dated 21.9.91. It appears from the written objection filed by the appellant before the Subordinate Judge that they have in paragraph-1 categorically asserted that the award dated 21.9.1991 given by the sole arbitrator Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan having had no existence or validity or legality in the eye of law and also being a nullity as the arbitrator was not appointed in this case in accordance with the terms of the Arbitration clause contained in the contract dated 3.9.1990, there cannot be any decree in terms of the award". On the question of jurisdiction or authority of the arbitrator Mr. Pal submitted that since the appellant had not taken any such objection before the arbitrator himself nor they had taken any such objection in the written objection before the learned Subordinate Judge, they have no right to agitate the same before this court for the first time. Unfortunately this submission of Mr. Pal is contrary to materials on record and is absolutely incorrect inasmuch as it appears that in paragraph 1 of the written objection the appellant have categorically agitated this point before the learned Subordinate Judge. It also appears from the impugned judgment that the learned Subordinate Judge did not advert to that point may be due to the fact that he found that the written objection filed by the appellant is no objection in the eye of law because it is barred by limitation as well as it is hit by section 33 of the Arbitration Act. Be that as it may, in our opinion, it is a question of law and it was incumbent upon the learned Subordinate Judge to look into the validity or legality of the award before making the same a rule of the court and he can enter into that arena of law even if no objection is taken by any one of the parties before him. We posed a question to Mr. Pal as to whether it is the duty of the court to consider the legal aspect of the case. Mr. Pal did not give any direct reply either in the affirmative or in the negative. He rather asserted that if a party does not take any such objection before the Subordinate Judge the Court has no authority to travel beyond the objections taken by the aggrieved party. We find it difficult to accept the submission of Mr. Pal on this point because it is a question of law and jurisdiction of the arbitrator is at stake. The whole fact of the award depends on the legality or validity of the appointment of the arbitrator. If in a particular case it is found that the arbitrator has not assumed jurisdiction as per law then any award given by him is void abinitio and a nullity in the eye of law. In the instant case the arbitration clause provides that if any party is dissatisfied with the decision given by the Additional Chief Engineer, the aggrieved party may write to the Chief Engineer of the Roads and High ways Department to appoint arbitrator/ arbitrators and he in accordance with clause B.6.31 will appoint arbitrator/ arbitrators to resolve the dispute. In the instant case it appears that after the cancellation of the instant contract dated 3.9.1990 the respondent wrote to the Additional Chief Engineer claiming compensation and when the Additional Chief Engineer asked the respondent to furnish supporting documents the respondent instead of complying with his direction wrote a letter to the Chief Engineer invoking the arbitration clause and requested him to appoint arbitrator and admittedly , the Chief Engineer did not appoint any arbitrator to resolve the dispute between the parties in the instant case. It appears to us that since the respondent has failed to comply with the request of the Additional Chief Engineer in that they have failed to furnish the supporting documents in support of their claims they had no right to invoke the arbitration clause in the instant case and to request the Chief Engineer to appoint an arbitrator in pursuance of clause B.6.31 of the contract dated 3.9.90. In that view of the matter the appointment of Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as their arbitrator appears to be premature as well as illegal inasmuch as no occasion has been as yet for referring the dispute to the arbitrator as the procedure laid down in clause B.6.31 of the contract has not been exhausted. Be that as it may, let us examine as to whether the sole arbitrator in the instant case assumed the jurisdiction legally or not. We have perused all the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1940 and we do not find any provision in the said Act which empowers an aggrieved party to appoint an arbitrator in the event of default by designated authority to appoint an arbitrator. The legal position is that if the designated authority fails to act in terms of the agreement in appointing the arbitrator then the aggrieved party can go to the civil court and file an application either under section 20 of the Arbitration Act or under section 8 of the Arbitration Act and request the Court to appoint an arbitrator to resolve the dispute. The present arbitration clause does not authorise the respondent to invoke section 8 of the Arbitration Act and appoint an arbitrator on their behalf in the event of failure on the part of the Chief Engineer to appoint an arbitrator in terms of clause B.6.31 of the contract. We have already found that the objection filed by the appellant be it under section 33 read with 30 or section 16 read with section 31 of the Arbitration Act is not an objection in the eye of law because of the non-compliance of the relevant provisions of the Act. In that view of the matter it was bounden duty of the learned Subordinate Judge to suo-motu inquire as to the validity or legality of the award before making the same as the rule of the court because jurisdiction goes at the root. In a case reported in 6 D.L.R.473 in which Mr. Pal was a party, it has been held that section 30 of the Arbitration Act contemplates misconduct of both the nature which makes the award invalid to be set aside under that section as well as misconduct which goes to the root of the matter and renders the award void which need not be avoided as it will be disregarded by each and every court, and if necessary, may be declared as such or set aside for the safety of the party affected thereby. In the latter case the court can and should take judicial notice of it and set it aside under section 17 of the Act suo motu without an application under section 30 of the Act within the period prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. Therefore, where an award is illegal and void, abinitio and the illegality is apparent on the fact of it, the court should take judicial notice of it, and it is not necessary that the parties should file objection to the award under section 30 within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act and in arriving at that finding their Lordships have relied on a decision of the privy Council reported in I.L.R. 13 (ALL) 300. In that case the award was filed beyond the period limited by the court. The party effected thereby objected to it. Their objection did not include the objection that it was filed beyond time and therefore invalid under section 521 of the Code of Civil Procedure of 1888 which declares that no award shall be valid unless made within the period allowed by the court. That objection was taken for the first time before their Lordships of the Privy Council. Their Lordships held : 

 11. We are in respectful agreement with the decisions reported in 6 DLR 478 and 8 DLR 305 and we do not find any reason to differ from those principles of law as laid down by their Lordships in those two decisions. In the facts and circumstance of the instant case it is crystal clear that the respondent has appointed Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as their arbitrator in violation of the provision of the arbitration clause as well as the provision of the Arbitration Act, 1940 and in that view of the matter the sole arbitrator Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan had no Jurisdiction in law to arbitrate upon the dispute between the parties in the instant case to resolve the dispute that had arisen between the parties due to unilateral cancellation of the agreement dated 3.9.1990 by the appellant and as such the award given by the learned arbitrator dated 21.9.1991 is void abinitio and a nullity in the eye of law. This vital legal aspect of the case way urged before the learned Subordinate Judge but he did not advert to that point and losing-sight of this legal aspect of the case the learned Subordinate Judge, in our opinion, has erroneously made the award dated 21. 9. 1991 as rule of the court, we therefore, find merits in this appeal. 

 12. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and order dated 30.11.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous case No. 71 of 1991 are set aside and the award dated 21.9.1991 signed and delivered by the learned arbitrator Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan is declared to be without jurisdiction and a nullity in the eye of law. 

 13. In the facts and circumstances of the case there will be no order as to cost.
